comments.value:
I would say this is a good idea, however. you will run into the same issue that Android and iOS have. they could have a shader converter yes, but it will be really broken. all custom shaders wouldnt work otherwise. In the end if they decide to support Linux. they would need to setup a shader converter or make it impossible to join windows-only worlds like Android.

Proton works well for now.

@{5f498858df2f180ebf64c3a5|full_name} If I understand correctly, Proton uses DXVK which is effectively what you're calling a "shader converter". Works fine though. I think AVPro Video and codecs is the more annoying thing.

@{613f4c103438830b78e68584|full_name} im meaning integrating that directly into the game, its not easy when it comes to unity honestly. or setting something up like the the iOS compatibility layer on android worlds that exists
I use Linux, yet I disagree. Proton works just fine. This is a bad idea, I'll leave it at that.

@{633050fb7dea1644bb2cc697|full_name} Proton does not work "just fine" players have issues even WITH custom patches to the Proton runtime. Moreover, most players aren't going to understand how to get these custom versions of Proton, nor even understand that these versions exist.

Moreover, a custom Linux version is not going to make the Windows build of the game just disappear.

i understand that it might be difficult at first (avatar compatibility worlds ect.) but proton has too many issues to ignore. id rather have less compatibility with worlds than not being able to use video players or the constant stuttering from proton.
I don't have much issues with proton, except for selfie expressions and some specific worlds. I would rather have a native build **only if** it's going to run smoother with less issues.
@{66b233a72f5b55a89c628a61|full_name} video players are almost always broken on it

@{5e59bc346312bf2d549f33ab|full_name}  They all work on my machine...

(okay maybe not all of them but most of them *work*)
The fact that the new steam frame is confirmed to be using linux is another reason this game needs a linux build.

I asked Tupper about this, and his response was essentially that Linux builds aren't feasible without adding quite a lot of complexity to shaders, since compiled shaders cannot simply be used on Linux without some way to translate them or recompile them on demand and that the former could be possible but Proton provides a sufficient enough experience that it'd be a waste of effort, and that the latter would be costly and potentially increase the size of avatars by 2-10x

Of course, Tupper can chime in and correct me if I'm wrong on this, but that's what I understood from my short conversation with them.

@{62770b2ab9aa4552a0459dc1|full_name} Proton is not viable without programs like Envision to fix reprojection and gain sufficient performance. SteamVR itself has fixed it's own issues for the most part but running VRChat through Proton via SteamVR is NOT VIABLE, It has major reprojection issues, it's like having serious double vision constantly. -And while yes, Envision exists, it's fragile and can break at any point. 

As for shaders, Vulkan has the capability to compile shaders from any platform but of course 3rd party shaders like Poiyomi, liltoon, and UTS2 might make DX11 calls, which would be the main issue. 

If that's the case, the best option would be to use DXVK to translate DX11 calls but I'm not sure how this could be implemented properly.
@{62770b2ab9aa4552a0459dc1|full_name} well how about they AT LEAST make it work properly on proton then? as every other update breaks a bunch of things, SPECIALLY the video player

Fully agreed. I tend to stay on Linux more than Windows. 

Proton works okay-ish, but it's not as good as when it's on Windows. Social, Invitations have never worked on my current setup. (help anyone)

I get absolutely plastered with in-app stuff to get VRC+, and I'm not going to pay one red cent for this unless native Linux support is finally treated seriously as a whole, from the app itself to VCC+Unity.  If it's shaders calling platform-specific stuff, you have the ability to require platform-agnostic support.

This all has been a complaint since the beginning and while I appreciate the small work that has been done in places, it really does need to be a co-priority with Windows+Android support.
second this. NEVER going to pay for vrc+ if they never bring proper linux support.
@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name} steam frame will be using linux, and the same price as quest so probably going to be more popular. WHEN will the devs give linux ANY proper support?

I'll add a +1 for a Native Linux Build, BUT having skimmed over a lot of the comments, I Have to laugh about a lot of it because so many comments are completely misunderstanding the complexity of what was already state by Tupper. Better linux support and considerations is already more than we can ask for. (Selfie cam fix when?) 

TL;DR Getting VRChat to run fully under proton is actually the better long term solution, DXVK Under Proton already does an amazing job of translating DX12 shaders to Vulkan and while A Native client would be amazing, the complexity of it does track. 

___ Rant ___

You can't "Just shim DXVK" in to the unity engine.

The shaders are compiled to binary form for Windows, 

- Mobile versions of the avatars use pre-defined potato shaders, that's why Mobile avis always have this hard limit on materials. 

Running VRChat under Proton works just fine, if you can't follow a simple guide on how to extract proton-GE-x-rtsp in to your steam's compatabilitytools.d folder then that's your skill issue. I'm sorry, but moving a file from folder A to folder B is one of the most basic of computer skills, there's no excuse if a guide tells you exactly where to place it.

IF you're using a broken compositor that can't render/pace frames properly, that's also a you problem - use software that doesn't suck (I'm calling out the ALVR and Steam VR combo for this one, it sucks right now i'm Sorry.)

@{66b3d90a08191275ad1a119c|full_name} It's getting really good already imo.

The last few months have been wonderful as a linux user of 1 year :)

No more issues with dj worlds or video player worlds on my end with latest ge rtsp.

Current setup: Cachyos, wivrn, ge rtsp, motoc and wayvr is all running smoother than ever now <3

With the steam frame coming out it's only going to get better
@{60296b864c9a9639a697f14d|full_name}It is! And i can't help but giggle a little that as of right now, youtube videos still work for me, but are broken for windows users ;) Proton magic!
@{60b2bc601ce9352da6a20e9d|full_name}Use the right version of proton then! https://github.com/SpookySkeletons/proton-ge-rtsp
@{66b3d90a08191275ad1a119c|full_name} It is the same for me lol

@{66b3d90a08191275ad1a119c|full_name}, the second part of your post is extremely tone deaf. The efforts should be in improving the experience on Proton, not on asking new players to follow these magical rituals. This is a big accessibility issue.

It *is* too much to ask players to install and use a custom version of Proton, a version that is maintained by a single person on their spare time. How would new players know that they need this? They wouldn't. They would think that VRChat is broken on Linux and leave it at that.

The best way to improve experience for everyone on Linux would be to upstream the Proton-RTSP patches to either Wine or Proton. That way everyone would benefit from them (possibly even outside of the VRChat ecosystem!). There may be reasons stopping them from doing this, that I don't know. What I know is that games should be something that works independent of your knowledge of computer mumbo jumbo.

@{5ad7ac4880e39f0da0bae4e9|full_name} No, it's not. That's Why we have forums and documentation. "RTFM - Read The F*ing Manual" is a skill everyone in every facet of life should have come to terms with by now whether you're working out how to use a microwave or assembling IKEA furniture. As a member of any community, especially this one it is everyone's responsibility Inform and Educate, not Hide it behind words like "Mumbo Jumbo" and expect someone else to bend to your whim. In an ideal world things should work flawlessly with default proton yes, but this world is not ideal and the reality is they sometimes don't and VRChat has some very niche and specific requirements that don't match the broad scope of Proton, this is why well established forks exist like Glorious Eggroll and for VRChat specifically, RTSP. 

If copying a folder from one place to another is too magical mumbo-jumbo for you personally then go ask someone who knows how to use a mouse to do it for you, but don't come at me with words like tone deaf when it's a skill issue on your part and all i've really done is lay out simple facts.

details: Official support for a native Linux build of VRChat. As Linux gaming continues to grow. More users are choosing Linux as their primary OS. A native build would provide better performance, lower overhead, improved compatibility for the growing Linux user base. This would be ensuring inclusivity for users across all platforms.
title: Native Linux Build
